nodes.name: scene_structure_targets
nodes.summary: Computes per-entity supervised targets (presence + nearest-distance bucket) for a world observation, using chebyshev_offsets to enumerate candidate cells and bucketing the minimum distance into n_distance_buckets classes.

nodes.name: balanced_class_weights
nodes.summary: Returns per-class weights normalized so present classes contribute equally to cross-entropy, guarding against divide-by-zero and unpresent classes; used to keep rare entity classes trainable.

nodes.name: variance_covariance_penalty
nodes.summary: VICReg-style anti-collapse penalty: hinge on per-dimension standard deviation below variance_gamma plus off-diagonal covariance-squared term, returning both components separately so the trainer can weight them independently.

nodes.name: ZWorldP0Config
nodes.summary: Dataclass carrying all training hyperparameters for ZWorldP0Trainer: loss weights (variance, covariance, presence, distance, proximity, resource-field, reconstruction, preservation), optimizer settings, and seed/holdout controls.

nodes.name: ZWorldP0Trainer
nodes.summary: Buffers world observations plus proximity/resource-field targets and jointly trains the agent's world encoder (plus skip and per-task heads) against scene structure, proximity, resource field, reconstruction, preservation, and VICReg-style anti-collapse losses, reporting holdout metrics.
nodes.languageNotes: Trainer owns its own optimizer and per-task heads (constructed lazily inside train()); relies on the agent's SelfEncoder-like object providing world_encoder, world_precision_logit, and optional world_skip attributes.

nodes.name: visitation.py
nodes.summary: Defines VisitationCounter, an unconditionally-allocated per-region visit-count tracker over a fixed-size FIFO anchor buffer in z_world. Deliberately distinct from FamiliarityTracker (an EMA) and the agent's raw visitation buffer, and kept out of scoring paths apart from one documented MECH-057b read.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors FamiliarityTracker's nearest-anchor kernel shape but stores exact counts; the module docstring records an explicit invariant about permitted consumers.

nodes.name: VisitationCounter
nodes.summary: Proximity-bucketed visit counter over a fixed-size FIFO anchor buffer in z_world, allocated unconditionally so visit counts are always available as telemetry.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Allocates the anchor buffer, per-anchor count vector and FIFO cursor for the configured world dimension, anchor count and kernel bandwidth.

nodes.name: _nearest_active
nodes.summary: Finds the nearest allocated anchor to a query point and its distance, the shared primitive behind both query and update.

nodes.name: query
nodes.summary: Returns the recorded visit count for the region containing a z_world point, or zero when no anchor lies within the bandwidth. Read-only.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Increments the count for the nearest in-bandwidth anchor, allocating a fresh anchor (overwriting the oldest when full) on first visit to a region.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Clears all anchors and counts back to the empty state, used between episodes or runs.

nodes.name: bla.py
nodes.summary: SD-035 basolateral-amygdala analogue: converts the z_harm_a affective stream into arousal-dependent hippocampal encoding gain (MECH-074a inverted-U), a content-selective per-trace retrieval bias vector (MECH-074b), and a harm-prediction-error remap signal gated by predictor attribution (MECH-074d). Peer module to the low-latency CeA analogue, operating on the hippocampal map rather than scalar salience channels.
nodes.languageNotes: Self-contained dataclass-config + stateful analogue pattern: BLAConfig (tuning constants sourced from cited neuroscience literature), BLAOutput (per-tick result record), and BLAAnalog (the stepping module). No project-internal imports, so the module is a leaf in the dependency graph.

nodes.name: BLAConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration record holding every BLA tuning constant: the inverted-U encoding-gain envelope (encoding_gain_max, encoding_gain_floor, arousal_threshold_on, arousal_peak), the post-event decay window, the retrieval-bias alpha and compensation terms, and the remap PE sigma threshold with its attribution gate.

nodes.name: BLAOutput
nodes.summary: Per-tick result record emitted by BLAAnalog.tick, carrying encoding_gain, the encoding-time arousal_tag, the per-trace retrieval_bias vector, the remap_signal, and the harm-PE diagnostics (magnitude, running baseline std, remaining encoding-window steps).

nodes.name: BLAAnalog
nodes.summary: Stateful basolateral-amygdala analogue stepped once per agent.sense(). Tracks harm-PE running statistics, the post-event encoding window, and emits encoding gain, arousal tagging, retrieval bias and remap decisions consumed by the hippocampal write and readout paths.

nodes.name: BLAAnalog.__init__
nodes.summary: Constructs the BLA analogue from an optional BLAConfig, validating and caching the arousal-threshold and inverted-U envelope parameters before delegating to reset for the mutable running state.

nodes.name: BLAAnalog.reset
nodes.summary: Clears all mutable per-episode state: the harm-PE running mean and standard deviation, the last encoding gain and arousal tag, and the remaining post-event encoding-window step counter.

nodes.name: BLAAnalog.tick
nodes.summary: Main per-step entry point: reads the z_harm_a affective stream and its one-step prediction, computes the inverted-U arousal-dependent encoding gain and its decay window, builds the content-selective per-trace retrieval bias vector from arousal tags, updates the harm-PE EMA baseline, and decides the attribution-gated remap signal before packaging everything into a BLAOutput.
nodes.languageNotes: Returns an early no-op BLAOutput (encoding_gain exactly 1.0) below arousal_threshold_on, which is the module's backward-compatibility contract when the feature flag is on but arousal is subthreshold.

nodes.name: BLAAnalog.diagnostics
nodes.summary: Returns the module's current internal counters (encoding-window steps remaining and related integer state) for experiment manifests and contract assertions.

nodes.name: test_task_claim_chip_mutations.py
nodes.summary: Contract test suite for the Phase-2 mutating claim and chip verbs in coordinator/db.py, exercising real SQLite files with injected clocks and real threads so the BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction semantics are actually under test.
nodes.languageNotes: Time-independent by construction: every verb takes an injected `now` and no assertion reads the wall clock; no mocks, because a mock would not reproduce the transaction semantics under test.

nodes.name: Base
nodes.summary: Shared unittest fixture: a real SQLite coordinator DB in a tempdir plus helpers to open a claim and read back its entry JSON.

nodes.name: TestOpen
nodes.summary: Contracts for try_open_task_claim -- row and resource writes, entry_json shape parity with the CLI, client-vs-server claimed_at stamping, rival arbitration, scope and stale exemptions, idempotency, and the threaded two-concurrent-opens race that replays the 2026-07-28 three-session collision.

nodes.name: TestCloseRenewAmend
nodes.summary: Contracts for the close, renew, amend and dedupe claim verbs: ambiguity refusals, note history preservation, the renewal ownership guard, and the composite primary key that makes byte-identical duplicates impossible.

nodes.name: TestChips
nodes.summary: Contracts for the chip ledger verbs -- record, claim, unclaim, resolve, attach, amend_prompt and amend_note -- covering the chip_ref marker requirement, the cross-host claim mutex and its stale supersession, human-note freezing, terminal-status guards, claim-note history accumulation, and archived-field handling.

nodes.name: TestScopeGuards
nodes.summary: Scope guards asserting db.py exposes no archive verb and that no verb writes git, keeping the DB layer free of the git plane.

nodes.name: _chip
nodes.summary: Builds a well-formed chip dict for the chip-ledger tests, with the chip_ref marker embedded in the prompt so record_chip accepts it.

nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: Stdlib-only HTTP coordinator service (http.server + sqlite3) exposing the bearer-token-authenticated fleet API: experiment claim arbitration, heartbeat/status ingest, the coordinator-authoritative TASK_CLAIMS/TASK_CHIPS mutation endpoints, and the WORKSPACE_STATE / recommendation-log / IGW-log submit queues.
nodes.languageNotes: Zero third-party dependencies by design: ThreadingHTTPServer plus sqlite3 on a minimal CX22 host, with every endpoint except /health gated behind a per-worker bearer token.

nodes.name: _canon
nodes.summary: Canonicalises an inbound machine label through machine_identity so fleet keys never diverge on hostname drift; an allowlist rather than a regex, because a worker's trailing digit is its identity.

nodes.name: auth_machine
nodes.summary: Resolves an Authorization bearer header to the machine label it was issued for, returning None when the token is unknown.

nodes.name: _tc_open
nodes.summary: POST /task_claim/open handler: validates the claim body and delegates to db.try_open_task_claim, whose check-and-insert transaction is the server-side arbitration that replaces the old read-then-write race.

nodes.name: _tc_close
nodes.summary: POST /task_claim/close handler: closes a claim by (session_id, claimed_at), refusing rather than guessing when a session holds several claims.

nodes.name: _tc_renew
nodes.summary: POST /task_claim/renew handler: moves a claim's claimed_at forward so a long-running session does not read as stale.

nodes.name: _tc_amend
nodes.summary: POST /task_claim/amend handler: replaces a closed claim's completion_note while preserving the prior text in completion_note_history.

nodes.name: _chip_claim
nodes.summary: POST /chip/claim handler: marks a chip as started by a specific session, so a chip that was merely recorded is never mistaken for one in progress.

nodes.name: _chip_resolve
nodes.summary: POST /chip/resolve handler: transitions a chip to done or withdrawn with an optional note and resolving session.

nodes.name: _chip_attach
nodes.summary: POST /chip/attach handler: binds a spawn_task task_id to an already-recorded chip_ref.

nodes.name: _chip_amend_prompt
nodes.summary: POST /chip/amend_prompt handler: corrects a stored chip prompt, refusing any text that does not carry the chip_ref marker required for self-reporting.

nodes.name: _chip_amend_note
nodes.summary: POST /chip/amend_note handler: appends an addendum to a chip's note, keeping the superseded text for audit.

nodes.name: _ws_append
nodes.summary: POST /workspace_state/append handler: queues a WORKSPACE_STATE.md entry into the DB for the materializer to render, rather than letting the client write git.

nodes.name: _reclog_append
nodes.summary: POST /recommendation_log/append handler: queues a recommendation-agreement ledger record for DB-authoritative materialization.

nodes.name: _igw_log_append
nodes.summary: POST /igw_log/append handler: queues an IGW routine-log line for materialization into the git-tracked log.

nodes.name: _intent_replace
nodes.summary: POST /git_intent handler: records a ree_commit.py intent record (declared paths, base sha, verdict) so a dropped-file push can be detected rather than slipping through.

nodes.name: _dispatcher_lease
nodes.summary: POST /dispatcher/lease handler: upserts a metaworker dispatcher run lease so only one box holds dispatch authority at a time.

nodes.name: _chip_episode
nodes.summary: POST /chip/episode handler: records a per-chip work episode (start/end, outcome) for metaworker learning.

nodes.name: _campaign_add
nodes.summary: POST /campaign/add handler: validates and inserts a dispatch campaign definition into the coordinator-authoritative campaign table.

nodes.name: _campaign_record_launch
nodes.summary: POST /campaign/launch handler: records a launch against a campaign, advancing its counters and launch history.

nodes.name: _campaign_status
nodes.summary: POST /campaign/status handler: sets a campaign's lifecycle status with an attributed actor and note.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Process entry point: loads tokens, opens the sqlite DB, and serves the ThreadingHTTPServer on the configured bind host and port.

nodes.name: Handler
nodes.summary: BaseHTTPRequestHandler subclass that owns the whole routing table: bearer auth, JSON body parsing, and the GET/POST dispatch to every claim, chip, heartbeat, queue, campaign and shadow-status endpoint.

nodes.name: task_claim_chip_git_writer.py
nodes.summary: The PHASE-2b DB-to-git materializer: the single git writer for TASK_CLAIMS.json, TASK_CHIPS.json, WORKSPACE_STATE.md, the recommendation log, the dispatcher control file and the dispatch-campaign registry, rendering each one from coordinator DB rows on a timer tick.
nodes.languageNotes: Each tick ingests origin before rendering so the render is a superset of origin's content by construction, which is what stops a fallback commit from being silently reverted.

nodes.name: _fetch_and_resolve
nodes.summary: Fetches origin and resolves the target branch to a sha, the read-only step every tick starts from.

nodes.name: _source_order
nodes.summary: Captures the source file's own row order so a client-side reorder is followed rather than rewritten into a spurious diff.

nodes.name: render_task_claims
nodes.summary: Renders TASK_CLAIMS.json from DB rows, preserving per-entry key order, row order, top-level metadata and any source entry the reconciler could not key, while applying the done-claim retention window.

nodes.name: render_chips
nodes.summary: Renders TASK_CHIPS.json from the chip-ledger rows, preserving source order and verbatim entry blobs; chips are never dropped by retention.

nodes.name: _ws_render_guards
nodes.summary: Guards a WORKSPACE_STATE.md render against truncation and misplaced insertion before the new text is allowed to replace the source.

nodes.name: render_workspace_state
nodes.summary: Inserts queued WORKSPACE_STATE entries at the correct block position, replacing the whole-file rewrite path that caused three silent-truncation incidents.

nodes.name: render_recommendation_log
nodes.summary: Renders queued recommendation-agreement records into the git-tracked ledger file.

nodes.name: ingest_dispatcher_control
nodes.summary: Reconciles the git-side dispatcher control document into the DB lease table before it is re-rendered.

nodes.name: render_dispatcher_control
nodes.summary: Renders the dispatcher control document from DB lease rows.

nodes.name: ingest_dispatch_campaigns
nodes.summary: Reconciles the git-side dispatch-campaign registry into the DB campaign table.

nodes.name: render_dispatch_campaigns
nodes.summary: Renders the dispatch-campaign registry from DB campaign rows.

nodes.name: ingest
nodes.summary: Reconciles both registry documents into the DB immediately before rendering, which is what closes the fallback-commit race a shadow-only timer cannot.

nodes.name: _writeback_rendered_base
nodes.summary: Records last_rendered_json for every row a render provably reached git with, giving the next ingest a base for its three-way merge instead of a blind adoption.

nodes.name: _semantic_delta
nodes.summary: Compares source and rendered documents on identifying key fields so a cosmetic difference is not reported as a real change.

nodes.name: materialize_once
nodes.summary: One full tick: fetch, ingest, render every managed document, decide whether anything materially changed, and in write mode commit, push with retry and write back the render base; check mode never moves anything.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: parses repo path, branch, mode and retry knobs and runs exactly one materialization tick, pacing owned by the systemd timer.

nodes.name: test_heartbeat_log.py
nodes.summary: Contract tests for the append-only heartbeat_log history table: a row is appended only on a state or current-experiment transition, the retention trim really deletes and is throttled, and the table is provisioned by a bare connect() as well as by init_db().

nodes.name: _Fixture
nodes.summary: Shared fixture giving each test a temporary sqlite database and a helper for reading back heartbeat_log rows.

nodes.name: TestTransitionLogging
nodes.summary: Pins that a heartbeat row is logged only on a genuine (state, current_exq) transition, independently per machine, with the payload stored verbatim and the latest-only heartbeats table left unaffected.

nodes.name: TestRetentionTrim
nodes.summary: Pins that the retention trim deletes rows past the window, honours a custom retention, no-ops on an empty table, and is throttled by a monotonic interval rather than running on every write.

nodes.name: TestTableProvisioning
nodes.summary: Pins that a bare connect() provisions heartbeat_log and its index on a fresh database and that init_db stays idempotent.

nodes.name: test_phase3_runpack_materialize.py
nodes.summary: Contract tests for the Phase-3 git writer's run-pack materialisation: a golden byte-shape check against a known good pack, back-filling a missing pack, never clobbering a runner-synced one, field-mapping precedence, and the default-off guarantee for the env knob.
nodes.languageNotes: Checkout-dependent tests skip rather than fail when no sibling REE_assembly checkout is present, which is the normal state inside a ree-v3 git worktree.

nodes.name: _resolve_ree_assembly
nodes.summary: Locates a real REE_assembly checkout as a sibling or via the env override, returning None so dependent tests skip rather than fail.

nodes.name: _make_flat
nodes.summary: Builds a synthetic flat manifest with the fields the run-pack converter reads, the input for every materialisation case.

nodes.name: GoldenByteShape
nodes.summary: Asserts the converter reproduces the canonical run pack for a real sibling run byte-for-byte, pinning the hub writer's output against the local governance converter.

nodes.name: MaterializeRunpacks
nodes.summary: Pins that a missing pack is back-filled and staged, an existing pack is never clobbered, non-eligible flats materialise nothing, and multiple flats are handled in one pass.

nodes.name: FieldMappingProvenance
nodes.summary: Pins the field-mapping precedence chain (top-level metrics over aggregates over readout) and that absent provenance or always-core fields are omitted rather than nulled.

nodes.name: FlagDefault
nodes.summary: Pins that run-pack materialisation stays off unless its env knob is explicitly set.

nodes.name: test_task_claim_chip_git_writer.py
nodes.summary: Contract tests for the PHASE-2b materializer tick against real git fixtures (bare remote plus working clone): round-trip byte equality, retention, the fallback-commit race, key-order fidelity, write-versus-check mode, source-order fidelity, and keyless-entry preservation.
nodes.languageNotes: Time-independent by construction: every retention assertion injects now_iso rather than reading the clock, so the suite cannot drift into flakiness at a window boundary.

nodes.name: _claim
nodes.summary: Builds a claim entry for the round-trip and retention fixtures.

nodes.name: _chip
nodes.summary: Builds a chip entry, including the unmodelled keys and odd key ordering the byte-equality contract depends on.

nodes.name: _seed_repo
nodes.summary: Seeds a working clone of a bare remote with both registry documents, so fetch, show, reset, commit and push exercise the real code paths.

nodes.name: _Fixture
nodes.summary: Shared fixture wiring a bare remote, a working clone and a DB, with helpers for running one tick and reading origin's text back.

nodes.name: TestRoundTripByteEquality
nodes.summary: Pins that ingesting a realistic file and rendering it back yields the exact same bytes, including unmodelled keys, non-alphabetical key order and a missing trailing newline.

nodes.name: TestRetention
nodes.summary: Pins that an aged-out done claim is dropped while the rest stays byte-exact, that a done entry without closed_at falls back to claimed_at, and that chips are never dropped.

nodes.name: TestFallbackCommitRace
nodes.summary: Pins that an entry committed straight to origin between ticks is ingested before rendering and therefore survives, so the render can never revert a fallback commit.

nodes.name: TestCoordinatorMutatedRows
nodes.summary: Pins that a coordinator-mutated row renders in the client's canonical key order and reaches origin in write mode.

nodes.name: TestWriteModeStateChangeOnly
nodes.summary: Pins that a matching tick commits nothing and a second write tick after a write is a no-op, so the writer produces no liveness-tick commits.

nodes.name: TestCheckModeNeverWrites
nodes.summary: Pins that a mismatch in check mode commits nothing and moves no ref.

nodes.name: TestSourceOrderFidelity
nodes.summary: Pins that a client-side file reorder is followed rather than rewritten, so merge machinery does not provoke a spurious full-file diff.

nodes.name: TestKeylessEntrySurvivesTheRender
nodes.summary: Pins that a source entry the reconciler cannot key is preserved at its source position, named rather than merely derivable, byte-stably and without resurrecting a retention drop.

nodes.name: TestNothingIsPreservedWhenTheDbHoldsEverything
nodes.summary: Pins that a healthy file preserves nothing extra and stays byte-stable, confirming the render is DB-driven rather than an echo of the source.

nodes.name: anchor_set.py
nodes.summary: Scale-tagged hippocampal anchor store implementing MECH-269 Phase 2, with dual-trace preservation (inactive anchors are retained rather than erased) and per-anchor hysteresis on V_s_anchor. Consumes MECH-288 BoundaryEvents to install and remap anchors keyed by (scale, segment_id, stream_mixture).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses frozen-style dataclasses plus a tuple AnchorKey type alias; torch is used only for cosine similarity over stored goal snapshots.

nodes.name: AnchorGoalPayload
nodes.summary: SD-039 dual-trace goal-snapshot payload attached to each anchor at write, remap or invalidation time, carrying z_goal_snapshot, wanting_strength, arousal_tag, last_vs and staleness_at_write.

nodes.name: Anchor
nodes.summary: A single scale-tagged anchor record holding its key, activity flag, hysteresis counters and optional goal payload, with a goal_match helper that scores cosine similarity against a current z_goal.

nodes.name: AnchorSet
nodes.summary: The anchor pool itself: writes and remaps anchors from boundary events, ticks per-anchor hysteresis on V_s minus staleness, marks outgoing anchors inactive instead of deleting them, and exposes active/all/dual-trace and goal-match query views.

nodes.name: ghost_goal_bank.py
nodes.summary: MECH-292 ranked ghost-goal bank: a read-only derived ranking view over the SD-039 dual-trace anchor pool that scores each anchor on a composite of wanting, goal match, staleness and recoverability, with optional MECH-339 outshining context gate and MECH-340 persistence/efficacy gate.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure arithmetic with no trainable parameters; all new behaviour is behind default-off config flags so the ranking is bit-identical to the pre-MECH-339 form by default.

nodes.name: PersistenceAppraisal
nodes.summary: Global appraisal pair (control_efficacy, goal_unattainability) in [0,1] supplied by the agent and used by the MECH-340 persistence licence gate.

nodes.name: GhostGoalBankEntry
nodes.summary: One ranked bank row: the source anchor key plus the per-channel scores (wanting, goal_match, staleness, recoverability, optional context term) and the combined ghost_priority.

nodes.name: GhostGoalBank
nodes.summary: Walks the anchor pool on each rank() call, applies the goal-match floor rumination guard, scores the additive dissociable channels, applies the outshining context gate and persistence licence, and returns a sorted ranked view plus diagnostics.

nodes.name: module.py
nodes.summary: The hippocampal planning module for REE V3: runs a CEM search over SD-004 action-object space (not raw z_world) to generate value-flat trajectory proposals, wiring in event segmentation, anchors, ghost goals, curiosity, visitation, residue terrain and invalidation broadcasts.
nodes.languageNotes: Per Q-020 ARC-007-strict the module deliberately has no value head: terrain sensitivity emerges from navigating a residue-shaped z_world, with all weighting introduced downstream in E3.

nodes.name: HippocampalModule
nodes.summary: Single large nn.Module orchestrating action-object CEM proposal generation, chunk and policy decomposition, curiosity/novelty bonuses, ghost-goal-seeded proposals, replay under hypothesis tagging, and the anchor/segmenter/invalidation tick paths.

nodes.name: dacc.py
nodes.summary: Implements the SD-032b dACC/aMCC-analog adaptive control module: a precision-weighted affective pain prediction error (MECH-258) plus recency/monostrategy suppression (MECH-260), integrated into a Croxson-style bundle of expected value, choice difficulty, foraging value and harm interaction. Explicitly an integrator rather than a selector -- a stopgap adapter converts the bundle into a per-candidate score bias for E3 until the SD-032a salience coordinator lands.
nodes.languageNotes: PyTorch nn.Module subclasses paired with a frozen-default dataclass config whose weights are all zero, so the module is a no-op unless explicitly activated -- the repo's standard default-off substrate pattern.

nodes.name: DACCConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding the sixteen tunable weights and bounds for the dACC analog (bundle gains, suppression memory, precision scale, effort cost, drive coupling, bias clamp, PE cap and the saturation sub-block). Every weight defaults to zero so an unconfigured instance is inert.

nodes.name: DACCAdaptiveControl
nodes.summary: The dACC/aMCC-analog control module itself: tracks affective prediction error against the E2_harm_a forward model with an EMA and saturation factor, records committed-action and outcome history to compute a monostrategy suppression penalty, and emits the integration bundle (mode_ev, choice_difficulty, foraging_value, harm_interaction) consumed downstream by action selection.

nodes.name: DACCtoE3Adapter
nodes.summary: Documented stopgap adapter that flattens the dACC bundle into a clamped per-candidate score bias E3.select() can consume directly, including the SD-057 L7 goal-readout term. Intended for removal once the SD-032a salience-network coordinator becomes the proper bundle consumer.

nodes.name: stuck_state_detector.py
nodes.summary: SD-061 stuck-state / impasse detector: fuses goal-progress stall, E3 score margin, committed-action-class diversity and dACC choice difficulty into a graded stuck_score plus binary is_stuck, gated by goal salience so it signals impasse rather than goal abandonment. Feeds the difficulty-gated proposal-entropy regulator that widens CEM proposals (MECH-343).
nodes.languageNotes: Pure-stdlib module (deque, dataclass) with no torch dependency; the module docstring carries an unusually detailed falsifiability record distinguishing it from adjacent mechanisms and documenting which axes empirically arrive at runtime.

nodes.name: StuckStateAxisUnavailable
nodes.summary: RuntimeError raised when an axis a run explicitly declared receives no input on a waking tick. Deliberately never swallowed, so a mis-wired detector refuses the run instead of silently rescaling the score over the surviving axes.

nodes.name: StuckStateDetectorConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass of the detector's fourteen knobs: per-axis windows and floors, the asymmetric EMA rise/fall rates, the stuck threshold, the mean-or-max combine mode, and the declared_axes mask with its grace period. Defaults keep the legacy mean-over-present-axes behaviour bit-identical.

nodes.name: StuckStateDetector
nodes.summary: The detector: validates its config up front, maps each present axis to a [0,1] deficit via four private helpers, combines them over the declared axis set, gates the result on goal salience, and drives an asymmetric EMA accumulator exposing stuck_score, is_stuck and per-axis presence counters. Simulation ticks (MECH-094) return the unchanged score without advancing state.

nodes.name: difficulty_gated_proposal_entropy.py
nodes.summary: SD-061 regulator that converts a stuck-state score into a transient widening of the CEM/hippocampal proposal layer (extra candidates plus a within-class sampling temperature lift), decaying as the impasse clears. Pure arithmetic, default-off, and identity-valued during simulation/replay so waking impasse cannot widen imagined proposals.
nodes.languageNotes: Dataclass config plus a plain (non-nn.Module) regulator class; the extensive module docstring records that the temperature half of the gain is inert unless the SD-055 differentiable-CEM consumer is enabled.

nodes.name: DifficultyGatedProposalEntropyConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass configuration for the SD-061 proposal-entropy regulator: master enable flag, maximum extra candidates, maximum fractional temperature gain, and a diagnostic-only flag recording whether the temperature lever had a live consumer.

nodes.name: DifficultyGatedProposalEntropy
nodes.summary: Waking-only regulator mapping a stuck_score in [0,1] onto an extra-candidate count and a within-class CEM temperature gain, with reset and diagnostic state reporting. Validates its config at construction and returns the identity gain under simulation_mode (MECH-094).

nodes.name: tonic_vigor.py
nodes.summary: MECH-320 tonic-vigor regulator: maintains a slow EWMA over realised E3 score receipts and emits an additive (or multiplicative) per-candidate score bias favouring action trajectories over no-op ones, gated by energy, drive and recent prediction error. Implements the mesolimbic-DA average-reward-rate / opportunity-cost account as a target-free directional bias at the E3 selection call site.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure-arithmetic regulator with no learned parameters; uses torch tensors only to build and clamp the per-candidate bias vector, and selects between additive and multiplicative forms via string tokens validated at construction.

nodes.name: TonicVigorConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass configuration for the MECH-320 tonic-vigor regulator: master switch, EWMA half-life, action/passive weights, bias clamp scale, the three secondary gate thresholds (energy, drive, prediction error), bias form, no-op class id, and the v_raw baseline mode.

nodes.name: TonicVigorOutput
nodes.summary: Dataclass carrying the regulator's per-call telemetry: the gated vigor scalar v_t, the maximum absolute bias applied, action/no-op candidate counts, and the three secondary gate values.

nodes.name: TonicVigor
nodes.summary: The MECH-320 regulator itself: update_score_receipt advances the slow EWMA over realised E3 scores, compute_score_bias builds the clamped per-candidate action-vs-no-op bias tensor, and three private gate helpers apply the energy, drive and prediction-error secondary modulators. Returns zeros and skips state advance under simulation_mode (MECH-094).

nodes.name: schema.sql
nodes.summary: Idempotent SQLite DDL applied at coordinator startup, defining the 16 tables that back the Phase-3 coordination plane: the experiment queue and results, per-machine heartbeats and the command channel, and the git-mirrored registries for task claims, chips, workspace-state appends and dispatch campaigns.
nodes.languageNotes: WAL journal mode with foreign keys ON; heavy use of CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS so the file can be re-applied on every boot, composite primary keys for the (session_id, claimed_at) claim key, and partial indexes (WHERE materialized_at IS NULL) to make pending-spool scans cheap.

nodes.name: experiments
nodes.summary: One row per experiment_queue.json item, keyed by queue_id, carrying priority, machine affinity, claim ownership and a lossless item_json copy. removal_reason/removed_at disambiguate an operator cancellation from a runner ERROR or a scientific FAIL, all of which otherwise land as status='completed'.

nodes.name: results
nodes.summary: One row per completed run, keyed by run_id so result delivery is idempotent under retries. Records the producing machine, the PASS/FAIL/ERROR outcome, manifest hash and size, and the commit time set by sync_daemon.

nodes.name: heartbeats
nodes.summary: Current telemetry snapshot per machine: last_seen, runner state, current experiment, progress and GPU payloads, and ETA fields. Machine shutdowns and runner-process exits are stored in deliberately separate column pairs so a process exit cannot overwrite the shutdown reason that arms the claim fence.

nodes.name: commands
nodes.summary: Remote-control command channel: one row per command issued to a machine (stop, pause, resume, kick, release_claim), with issue and acknowledgement timestamps so a runner can drain the pending set on each loop tick.

nodes.name: heartbeat_log
nodes.summary: Append-only history of heartbeat state transitions per machine, retaining the observed time, the transition label, the current experiment and the raw payload for after-the-fact fleet forensics.

nodes.name: claim_log
nodes.summary: Shadow-mode audit trail comparing the coordinator's claim decision against the git-based verdict for each queue_id, with a diverged flag and free-text detail. Indexed on divergence so the soak criterion is a single cheap query.

nodes.name: task_claims
nodes.summary: Mirror of TASK_CLAIMS.json claims[], with a deliberately composite primary key of (session_id, claimed_at) because one session id can own several claims. Keeps status, closed_at, an append-only completion_note_history_json and a lossless entry_json.

nodes.name: task_claim_resources
nodes.summary: Child table holding each claim's resource paths as rows rather than a JSON column, so rival-claim lookup during arbitration is one indexed SELECT inside a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction instead of a whole-table JSON scan. Cascades on delete from task_claims.

nodes.name: chip_ledger
nodes.summary: Mirror of TASK_CHIPS.json chips[], keyed by chip_ref because task_id is null until someone clicks the chip. Carries title/tldr/prompt (nulled once archived into archived_json), origin and claim provenance, and resolution fields.

nodes.name: task_claim_chip_drift_log
nodes.summary: Per-check self-consistency record for the claim/chip git mirror, counting new, updated, orphan and retired keys on both sides plus a diverged flag. It is the durable evidence for the Phase-1 'N days of zero drift' exit criterion.

nodes.name: workspace_state_entries
nodes.summary: Append-only spool for WORKSPACE_STATE.md entries submitted by clients; the registry materializer splices pending rows into the live file byte-preservingly and stamps materialized_at/materialized_ref once the text provably reached git. No edit or delete verb exists.

nodes.name: recommendation_log_entries
nodes.summary: Append-only spool for recommendation-agreement ledger records, storing the client's exact bytes plus submission and materialization provenance, with a partial index over rows not yet materialized into git.

nodes.name: dispatcher_leases
nodes.summary: One row per dispatcher holding a run lease, with a lossless entry_json rendered verbatim into dispatcher_control.json. Git-side writes are ingested upsert-if-newer so the file stays a degraded fallback that still carries an emergency stop when the hub is unreachable.

nodes.name: igw_log_entries
nodes.summary: Append-only spool for the IGW routine tick's single-line heartbeat entries. Same contract as the other append tables, but rendered by a dedicated REE_assembly writer because this target file lives in a different repository.

nodes.name: git_intent_log
nodes.summary: Purely observational audit trail for the generic whole-file compare-and-swap verb POST /intent/replace, recording repo, path, base and applied shas, the verdict and before/after sizes. Intents are applied synchronously, so there is no pending row shape here.

nodes.name: dispatch_campaigns
nodes.summary: Dispatch campaign ledger mirroring scripts/dispatch_campaigns.json, one row per campaign with status, expiry and a lossless entry_json. Launch recording is decided inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE so two cloud dispatchers cannot claim the same campaign.

nodes.name: phase3_preflight.py
nodes.summary: Stage-aware health gate for the Phase 3 coordinator cutover: probes the hub over SSH and HTTP, classifies the deployment stage (pre-cutover, post-cutover or auto) and renders a blocking/advisory verdict with ASCII-only output. Exit code 0 means no blocking check failed, 1 a blocking failure, 2 a configuration error.
nodes.languageNotes: The module docstring is an in-line design record: the original always-FAIL verdict defect and the stage concept that fixed it are explained where the code lives, so the polarity flip on hub_sync_mode_safe cannot be 'simplified' away without reading why it exists.

nodes.name: CheckResult
nodes.summary: Value object carrying one preflight check's name, status (PASS/FAIL/WARN/SKIP), detail text and whether the check is blocking for the resolved deployment stage.

nodes.name: _load_env_file
nodes.summary: Parses a coordinator.env style key=value file into a dict, tolerating comments and blank lines.

nodes.name: _ssh_run
nodes.summary: Runs a remote command on the hub over SSH with a timeout, returning stdout plus an error string; honours dry-run by reporting the command without executing it.

nodes.name: _http_get
nodes.summary: Performs an authenticated GET against a coordinator endpoint with a bearer token and returns the decoded JSON body or an error string.

nodes.name: _run_check_shadow
nodes.summary: Probes the coordinator's /shadow/status endpoint and converts the response into a check outcome describing reachability and shadow state.

nodes.name: _import_sync_daemon_ready
nodes.summary: Imports the local sync daemon module to read the PHASE3_GIT_WRITER_READY flag, providing the fallback stage signal used when the hub could not be probed.

nodes.name: _observed_sync_mode
nodes.summary: Classifies the raw SYNC_MODE string read from the hub into a normalised observed mode (coordinator, authoritative or unknown).

nodes.name: _resolve_stage
nodes.summary: Resolves the deployment stage from, in precedence order, an explicit flag, the hub's observed SYNC_MODE, and finally the local writer-ready flag, returning both the stage and the signal that decided it.

nodes.name: _evaluate_hub_sync_mode
nodes.summary: Adjudicates the hub_sync_mode_safe check with stage-dependent polarity: blocking against authoritative mode pre-cutover, blocking against a regression to coordinator mode post-cutover, and purely advisory when the stage was auto-inferred from the same probe.
nodes.languageNotes: The advisory case exists to avoid circular reasoning: inferring the stage from a probe and then blocking on that same probe would make the check self-confirming.

nodes.name: _evaluate_fleet_lifecycle
nodes.summary: Evaluates fleet machine lifecycle state (including the retired hub runner and the set of peers that need waking) and produces the one check that stays blocking in every deployment stage.

nodes.name: run_preflight
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the whole preflight run: loads configuration, executes every local, SSH and HTTP probe (or their mock/dry-run stand-ins), resolves the stage and returns the structured summary of all checks.

nodes.name: _summary
nodes.summary: Aggregates individual check results into the summary dict carrying the overall ok flag, blocking-failure count, stage and the signal that resolved the stage.

nodes.name: _verdict_lines
nodes.summary: Builds the human-readable verdict block, phrasing the top line and its remediation advice according to the resolved stage and which checks were blocking.

nodes.name: _print_report
nodes.summary: Prints the per-check report and verdict to stdout in ASCII-only form, marking advisory checks distinctly from blocking ones.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry point: parses the stage, dry-run, mock, cutover-window, JSON and quiet flags, rejects mutually exclusive stage combinations, runs the preflight and maps the verdict onto the process exit code.

nodes.name: test_phase3_preflight.py
nodes.summary: Hermetic smoke and unit tests for phase3_preflight.py that never touch a live hub: they strip every COORDINATOR_URL source from the environment, exercise the CLI via subprocess, and unit-test the pure stage/polarity helpers with faked probe results.
nodes.languageNotes: The suite loads the module under test by path (_import_preflight) rather than by package import, so it works whether or not coordinator/ is importable as a package.

nodes.name: _hermetic_env
nodes.summary: Builds a subprocess environment with COORDINATOR_URL, COORDINATOR_TOKEN and COORDINATOR_ENV_FILE removed, which is what actually keeps a test off the live hub since --env-file alone is not sufficient.

nodes.name: test_mock_json_all_pass_structure
nodes.summary: Asserts that a --mock --json run emits a well-formed summary object in which every check passes.

nodes.name: test_dry_run_local_checks
nodes.summary: Exercises a --dry-run invocation end to end and verifies that the local checks execute while remote probes are reported rather than performed.

nodes.name: test_cutover_window_flag_accepted
nodes.summary: Confirms the --cutover-window flag is accepted by the CLI, preserving the exact semantics deploy/phase3_cutover.sh depends on.

nodes.name: test_evaluate_fleet_lifecycle_pure
nodes.summary: Unit-tests _evaluate_fleet_lifecycle as a pure function over synthetic machine records, checking the pass/fail classification of fleet lifecycle states.

nodes.name: test_evaluate_fleet_lifecycle_hub_runner_retired
nodes.summary: Pins the retired-hub-runner behaviour so the lifecycle check does not flag the deliberately disabled hub runner as a fault.

nodes.name: test_wake_fleet_needed_set_matches_lifecycle_peers
nodes.summary: Checks that the set of machines reported as needing a wake is exactly the set of lifecycle peers, so the two views cannot drift apart.

nodes.name: test_local_modes_do_not_need_coordinator_env
nodes.summary: Verifies that --dry-run and --mock complete without any coordinator environment configuration, which is what makes the suite runnable off the fleet.

nodes.name: test_live_mode_still_fails_without_url
nodes.summary: Asserts a live (non-mock) run without COORDINATOR_URL exits with the configuration-error code rather than silently degrading.

nodes.name: _import_preflight
nodes.summary: Loads phase3_preflight.py as a module directly from its file path so the pure helpers can be unit-tested without a package import.

nodes.name: test_observed_sync_mode_classification
nodes.summary: Unit-tests the normalisation of raw SYNC_MODE strings into the coordinator / authoritative / unknown classification.

nodes.name: test_resolve_stage_signal_precedence
nodes.summary: Pins the precedence order of stage signals: an explicit flag beats the hub's observed mode, which beats the local writer-ready flag.

nodes.name: test_evaluate_hub_sync_mode_three_polarities
nodes.summary: Covers all three polarities of the hub_sync_mode_safe check -- blocking pre-cutover, inverted post-cutover, advisory under auto stage inference.

nodes.name: _fake_probes
nodes.summary: Monkeypatches the preflight module's SSH and HTTP probe functions with deterministic stand-ins parameterised by sync mode, fleet lifecycle and writer readiness.

nodes.name: test_authoritative_hub_no_longer_forces_a_fail_verdict
nodes.summary: Regression test for the always-FAIL verdict defect: an authoritative hub under auto stage inference must no longer force a blocking failure.

nodes.name: test_pre_cutover_gate_still_gates
nodes.summary: Confirms the original pre-cutover gate semantics survive the stage refactor: an authoritative hub still blocks under --pre-cutover.

nodes.name: test_cutover_window_implies_pre_cutover
nodes.summary: Asserts --cutover-window implies the pre-cutover stage, so the deployment script keeps its prior behaviour unchanged.

nodes.name: test_post_cutover_pinned_catches_a_regressed_hub
nodes.summary: Verifies the inverted post-cutover polarity: a hub that has fallen back to coordinator mode is reported as a blocking regression.

nodes.name: test_fleet_lifecycle_stays_blocking_in_every_stage
nodes.summary: Pins the invariant that fleet_lifecycle remains a blocking check regardless of which deployment stage was resolved.

nodes.name: test_stage_falls_back_to_the_local_writer_flag_when_hub_unprobed
nodes.summary: Exercises the fallback path where the hub could not be probed and the stage must be inferred from the local PHASE3_GIT_WRITER_READY flag.

nodes.name: test_json_carries_stage_and_blocking_fields
nodes.summary: Pins the machine-readable contract: the --json payload must carry the resolved stage and per-check blocking flags for downstream consumers.

nodes.name: test_report_marks_advisory_checks
nodes.summary: Checks that the printed report visibly distinguishes advisory checks from blocking ones, so a reader cannot mistake an advisory FAIL for a gate.

nodes.name: causal_grid_world.py
nodes.summary: The V3 experimental environment: a 2D grid world with persistent agent causal footprint whose observation is split into proprioceptive body_state and exteroceptive world_state channels to match the SD-005 z_self/z_world latent split. Also hosts hazard/resource proximity gradient fields, microhabitat zones, weather and transient events, landmarks, subgoal waypoints and the effort-dissociation layout used across the experiment suite.
nodes.languageNotes: Class members are content-hashed (_member_source/_group_hash) and constructor arguments stably repr'd (_stable_repr) to produce a config_hash that answers 'is this the same environment configuration?'. The seed is excluded on purpose so two seeds of one experiment stay comparable; the run_id already identifies a single run.

nodes.name: CausalGridWorld
nodes.summary: The grid-world environment itself: five discrete actions over a 2D grid with health, energy and a persistent contamination footprint, returning observations as both a channel dict and a flat tensor, and labelling each transition with ground-truth causal attribution (agent_caused_hazard, env_caused_hazard, resource, waypoint and others) for SD-003.
nodes.languageNotes: All environment randomness flows through a single seeded numpy Generator, so every stochastic subsystem (weather, drift, respawn, zone sampling) is reproducible across runs -- a prerequisite for the novelty/curiosity claims that consume this environment's prediction error.

nodes.name: CausalGridWorldV2
nodes.summary: Factory that constructs a CausalGridWorld with proxy-gradient fields enabled, exposing the hazard and resource proximity gradients plus the harm_obs / harm_obs_a interoceptive streams. Its docstring carries the stochastic-attractor audit classifying every RNG draw as predictable-stochastic or irreducibly random.

nodes.name: _member_source
nodes.summary: Returns the source text of one hashed class member, falling back to repr() for class-level constants that have no retrievable source.

nodes.name: _stable_repr
nodes.summary: Produces deterministic text for a constructor argument, normalising dicts and sets by sorted key/element and hashing numpy arrays by content, so the config hash is stable across constructions.

nodes.name: db.py
nodes.summary: SQLite persistence layer for the experiment coordinator: schema migrations, atomic experiment-claim arbitration, machine heartbeats and lifecycle, and the authoritative task-claim / chip-ledger / workspace-state / dispatch-campaign registries.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-process writer design: WAL mode plus explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions around conditional UPDATEs make claim arbitration atomic without any external mutex. All printed text is kept ASCII-only for Windows cp1252 safety.

nodes.name: task_claim_chip_shadow_sync.py
nodes.summary: Phase-1 shadow reconciliation tick that reads TASK_CLAIMS.json and TASK_CHIPS.json from an authoritative git ref of the umbrella repo and converges the coordinator DB mirror to match. Deliberately read-only: it never mutates a git working tree or ref.
nodes.languageNotes: Designed for structural incapability rather than discipline: every git invocation is fetch/rev-parse/show, so the module cannot produce the autostash/rebase failure class the migration exists to remove. Run as a systemd oneshot from a timer.

nodes.name: test_registry_ingest_authority.py
nodes.summary: Contract tests pinning the Phase-2b ingest authority fix: a three-way merge with a recorded render base so coordinator-side claim closures and chip resolutions survive re-ingest of stale git rows, while genuine git-path mutations are still adopted.

nodes.name: test_task_claim_chip_shadow_sync.py
nodes.summary: Contract tests for the Phase-1 shadow reconciliation tick, using real throwaway git repositories to pin ref-only reads, idempotent no-op ticks, structural git-mutation incapability, and skip-rather-than-fallback behaviour on an unresolvable ref.

nodes.name: connect
nodes.summary: Opens the coordinator SQLite database with WAL mode and the pragmas required for the single-writer atomic-claim design.

nodes.name: _migrate_task_claim_chip_tables
nodes.summary: Creates and forward-migrates every table backing the task-claim, claim-resource and chip-ledger registries, including the last_rendered_json merge base column.

nodes.name: upsert_task_claim
nodes.summary: Ingests a task-claim entry from a rendered git document into the DB mirror, merging against the recorded render base so coordinator-side mutations are not clobbered.

nodes.name: upsert_chip
nodes.summary: Ingests a chip-ledger entry from git into the DB mirror using the same three-way merge against the recorded render base as claims.

nodes.name: reconcile_task_claims
nodes.summary: Reconciles the whole task-claim mirror against a source document in one tick, reporting per-entry unchanged / updated / diverged counts.

nodes.name: reconcile_chips
nodes.summary: Reconciles the chip-ledger mirror against a source document and returns the same per-entry outcome tally as claim reconciliation.

nodes.name: log_task_claim_chip_drift
nodes.summary: Records a drift observation row for one reconciliation tick so mirror divergence can be audited over time.

nodes.name: task_claim_chip_drift_summary
nodes.summary: Aggregates recorded drift rows into a windowed summary used by status endpoints and drift dashboards.

nodes.name: try_open_task_claim
nodes.summary: Atomically arbitrates a new task claim: checks rival active claims on file-shaped resources inside one immediate transaction and inserts only if this session wins.

nodes.name: close_task_claim
nodes.summary: Closes an open task claim, recording closed_at and the completion note, and refusing when the session id is ambiguous.

nodes.name: renew_task_claim
nodes.summary: Extends the lifetime of an active task claim, refreshing staleness stamps without disturbing the claim's identity key.

nodes.name: amend_task_claim
nodes.summary: Replaces a closed claim's completion note while preserving the prior text in completion_note_history.

nodes.name: record_chip
nodes.summary: Registers a spawned chip in the ledger with its chip_ref, title, tldr and verbatim prompt so it survives the spawning session.

nodes.name: try_claim_chip
nodes.summary: Atomically claims an open chip for a session, refusing when another session already holds it.

nodes.name: unclaim_chip
nodes.summary: Releases a chip claim back to the open pool, leaving the ledger row and its history intact.

nodes.name: resolve_chip
nodes.summary: Marks a chip done or withdrawn with a resolution note, recording the terminal state that later ingests must never downgrade.

nodes.name: attach_chip
nodes.summary: Attaches a spawn task id to an existing chip_ref without implying the chip has been started.

nodes.name: amend_chip_prompt
nodes.summary: Replaces a chip's stored prompt, enforcing the chip_ref marker requirement and archiving the prior text in prompt_history.

nodes.name: amend_chip_note
nodes.summary: Amends a chip's note while preserving the previous value, mirroring the claim completion-note amendment semantics.

nodes.name: submit_workspace_state_entry
nodes.summary: Queues a WORKSPACE_STATE.md Recent Work entry for the materializer to render, replacing direct whole-file rewrites.

nodes.name: submit_recommendation_log_entry
nodes.summary: Queues a recommendation-agreement ledger entry for later materialization into the git-tracked log.

nodes.name: submit_igw_log_entry
nodes.summary: Queues an IGW routine log entry for materialization, keeping the exposed ledger file off the direct write path.

nodes.name: record_git_intent
nodes.summary: Records a git commit intent (declared paths and blobs) so a pre-push guard can detect a silently dropped file.

nodes.name: upsert_dispatcher_lease
nodes.summary: Grants or refreshes a dispatcher run lease for a worker machine, the record the dispatcher control materializer renders.

nodes.name: _campaign_validate
nodes.summary: Validates a dispatch-campaign payload's required fields, types and status enum before any write is attempted.

nodes.name: add_campaign
nodes.summary: Inserts a new dispatch campaign after validation, rolling back cleanly on any constraint failure.

nodes.name: record_campaign_launch
nodes.summary: Records a launch against a live campaign, bumping its version and refusing launches on expired or terminal campaigns.

nodes.name: set_campaign_status
nodes.summary: Transitions a campaign's status with validation and optimistic version bumping.

nodes.name: record_chip_episode
nodes.summary: Records a chip execution episode (dispatch, outcome and timing) for metaworker campaign accounting.

nodes.name: init_db
nodes.summary: Runs every migration in order against a connection, the single entry point callers use to provision the schema.

nodes.name: upsert_experiment
nodes.summary: Inserts or updates a queue item row from the queue snapshot, canonicalising machine affinity along the way.

nodes.name: _claim_recoverable
nodes.summary: Decides whether a stale experiment claim may be recovered, combining the time floor with positive departure evidence rather than mere heartbeat absence.

nodes.name: claim_fence_active
nodes.summary: Reports whether a machine's claim fence is armed, blocking re-claims after an announced shutdown.

nodes.name: machine_departed
nodes.summary: Determines whether a machine has positively departed, the non-time-based route to releasing its experiment claim without risking a duplicate run.

nodes.name: try_claim
nodes.summary: Atomically claims a queue item for a machine using a conditional UPDATE inside an immediate transaction, serialising all competing runners.

nodes.name: release_claim
nodes.summary: Releases a machine's experiment claim and records the reason, returning the item to the claimable pool.

nodes.name: upsert_heartbeat
nodes.summary: Records a machine heartbeat with progress telemetry and logs material state transitions for the live-status writers.

nodes.name: record_shutdown_notice
nodes.summary: Records a machine's positive shutdown signal and arms its claim fence, the evidence that makes departure-based claim recovery safe.

nodes.name: lifecycle_state
nodes.summary: Derives a machine's current lifecycle state (live, announced offline, departed) from heartbeats and shutdown notices.

nodes.name: ack_command
nodes.summary: Acknowledges a queued remote-control command, recording its result and closing the command channel round trip.

nodes.name: _resolve_and_fetch
nodes.summary: Fetches and resolves the configured authoritative git ref read-only, returning None when it cannot be resolved so the tick is skipped rather than falling back to the working tree.

nodes.name: _show_json
nodes.summary: Reads one JSON document out of a git ref via `git show` and parses it, never touching the working tree.

nodes.name: load_source_documents
nodes.summary: Loads TASK_CLAIMS.json and TASK_CHIPS.json from the resolved ref, returning None when neither file exists anywhere.

nodes.name: reconcile_once
nodes.summary: Performs one reconciliation tick: load both source documents from the ref, reconcile the DB mirror tables, and log the resulting drift row.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that parses repo/ref/database options and runs a single oneshot reconciliation tick for the systemd timer.

nodes.name: IngestAuthorityBase
nodes.summary: Shared in-memory database fixture providing the pure-DB seam the ingest-authority contracts exercise without any git repository.

nodes.name: TestClaimIngestAuthority
nodes.summary: Pins claim-side merge semantics: a coordinator close survives re-ingest of a stale active git row, a genuine git-path close is adopted, and a terminal state is never downgraded when no base exists.

nodes.name: TestChipIngestAuthority
nodes.summary: Mirrors the claim contracts on the chip ledger: a DB-side resolve survives re-ingest, and chip claims are adopted or preserved depending on which side diverged from the base.

nodes.name: TestMigrationAndWriteback
nodes.summary: Covers the render-writeback round trip that records the merge base, confirming a mutation after writeback survives re-ingest of the render's own text.

nodes.name: _Fixture
nodes.summary: Test fixture wiring a bare remote, a seeded umbrella clone and a coordinator database for the shadow sync contracts.

nodes.name: TestReconcileOnce
nodes.summary: Pins that a tick reads both registries from the git ref, reconciles them together, is a no-op on repeat, and picks up source-side edits.

nodes.name: TestStructuralIncapability
nodes.summary: Asserts that no git-mutating command is ever invoked: the tick leaves the source working tree, index and refs untouched whatever the outcome.

nodes.name: TestDegradePath
nodes.summary: Pins the skip-rather-than-fallback behaviour when the ref cannot be fetched or resolved, the regression that once ingested a three-week-old working tree.

nodes.name: TestDriftLogIntegration
nodes.summary: Confirms a tick with nothing to read returns None instead of writing a misleading all-zero drift row.

nodes.name: agent.py
nodes.summary: Defines REEAgent, the V3 substrate's central integration point: it wires the latent stack, E1/E2/E3 predictors, hippocampal, residue, affect, PFC and sleep subsystems into a single multi-rate sense-predict-select-act-residue loop. Effectively the whole cognitive architecture in one 13k-line module.
nodes.languageNotes: A PyTorch nn.Module whose __init__ alone spans ~3100 lines of conditional subsystem construction; most architectural claims (MECH-*/SD-*/ARC-*) are wired here behind config flags rather than in separate composition code.

nodes.name: AgentState
nodes.summary: Dataclass snapshot of the agent's state at one timestep: latent state, precision, running variance, step, accumulated harm, commitment/beta flags and optional serotonergic state.

nodes.name: REEAgent
nodes.summary: The REE V3 agent: an nn.Module implementing the multi-rate REE loop (sense, E1/E2/E3 ticks, trajectory selection, action, residue accumulation, replay and offline/sleep integration) plus every subsystem hook the architectural claims are tested through.
nodes.languageNotes: 106 methods on one nn.Module subclass; subsystem activation is almost entirely config-gated, so most branches are inert at production defaults.

nodes.name: candidate_support_preflight
nodes.summary: Computes diagnostic first-action support metrics over a candidate trajectory set so callers can decide whether a behavioural interpretation is admissible.

nodes.name: _resolve_chunk_deliberation_horizon
nodes.summary: Resolves the MECH-323 chunk ceiling's deliberation horizon, mirroring the hippocampal rollout horizon unless a sentinel-defaulted config override is set.

nodes.name: REEAgent.__init__
nodes.summary: Constructs every V3 subsystem the agent can run -- latent stack, E1/E2/E3 predictors, hippocampal module, residue field, clocks, affect/PFC/sleep components -- gating each on the REEConfig flags.

nodes.name: REEAgent.from_config
nodes.summary: Factory constructing an REEAgent from a configuration object.

nodes.name: REEAgent.reset
nodes.summary: Resets the agent to episode start: clears latent state, buffers, residue-adjacent counters and every subsystem's per-episode state.

nodes.name: REEAgent.sense
nodes.summary: Splits an observation into body and world channels and drives the resulting encodings through the latent stack and downstream perceptual subsystems.

nodes.name: REEAgent._e1_tick
nodes.summary: Runs the E1 deep-predictor tick and pushes the resulting z_self/z_world into the theta buffer.

nodes.name: REEAgent._e3_tick
nodes.summary: Runs the E3 tick, consuming the theta-cycle summary and driving hippocampal proposal generation.

nodes.name: REEAgent.generate_trajectories
nodes.summary: Produces candidate action trajectories for E3 evaluation via the hippocampal proposer.

nodes.name: REEAgent.select_action
nodes.summary: The selection core: scores candidate trajectories with E3 (harm evaluation, precision, curiosity and modulatory routes), applies gating, and commits to an action while recording extensive diagnostics.

nodes.name: REEAgent.act
nodes.summary: Executes one agent step: senses, ticks the rates, selects and returns the action to run in the environment.

nodes.name: REEAgent._do_replay
nodes.summary: Triggers hippocampal replay on quiescent E3 cycles, tagging all replayed content as hypothesis.

nodes.name: REEAgent.update_residue
nodes.summary: Accumulates world-delta into the persistent residue field under the MECH-094 hypothesis-tag gate.

nodes.name: REEAgent.record_transition
nodes.summary: Records an environment transition into the agent's learning buffers.

nodes.name: REEAgent.update_z_goal
nodes.summary: Updates the goal latent and super-ordinal goal memory from current context, drives and schema state.

nodes.name: REEAgent.compute_e2_loss
nodes.summary: Computes the E2 fast-predictor motor-sensory prediction loss.

nodes.name: REEAgent.offline_integration
nodes.summary: Runs a sleep-like offline integration pass over accumulated residue and replay material.

nodes.name: REEAgent.run_sleep_cycle
nodes.summary: Runs a full sleep cycle -- SWS schema pass followed by REM attribution pass -- and restores online mode.

nodes.name: REEAgent._assemble_control_vector
nodes.summary: Assembles the control/modulatory vector consumed by downstream selection and gating from precision, drive, affect and neuromodulatory state.

nodes.name: REEAgent.get_state
nodes.summary: Returns an AgentState snapshot of the agent's current timestep state.

nodes.name: serotonin.py
nodes.summary: Implements the tonic 5-HT (serotonin) state variable for REE-v3, modelling benefit-salience tagging and the REM gate zero-point across wake/SWS/REM phases. Dynamically modulates goal seeding gain and valence wanting floor, and is default-off behind a master switch.
nodes.languageNotes: Dataclass config paired with a stateful module class -- the dominant configuration pattern across ree_core.

nodes.name: SerotoninConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding the serotonin module's tunable parameters: rise/decay/harm-suppression rates, baseline tonic level, seeding-gain and wanting-floor modulation ranges, and the default-off master switch.

nodes.name: SerotoninModule
nodes.summary: Stateful tonic 5-HT accumulator that rises with benefit exposure, decays toward baseline, and is suppressed by harm; exposes benefit/harm salience tags, sleep-phase transitions (SWS/REM/wake) and REM-entry precision capture.

nodes.name: e3_selector.py
nodes.summary: The E3 trajectory selector: scores candidate action trajectories over z_world using harm evaluation, goal error and residue cost, and owns dynamic precision derived from its own prediction-error variance. This is the primary action-selection and commitment locus of the V3 substrate.
nodes.languageNotes: A very large single-class module (~4400 lines) with PyTorch tensor operations throughout; module-level helper functions are pure and independently testable.

nodes.name: SelectionResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass carrying the outcome of one trajectory selection: the chosen trajectory, its score components and the commitment/precision telemetry attached to the decision.

nodes.name: E3TrajectorySelector
nodes.summary: Core selector class that evaluates harm over z_world, tracks running prediction-error variance to derive commit thresholds and precision, applies residue and goal terms to the scoring equation, and emits the committed trajectory.

nodes.name: project_channel_range
nodes.summary: Projects a feature tensor's channel range into the selector's working representation, normalising per-channel extents before scoring.

nodes.name: authority_spread_ratio
nodes.summary: Computes the ratio between a lever's influence and the dominant authority basis, quantifying how contested control of the selection is.

nodes.name: authority_ratio_is_competitive
nodes.summary: Predicate deciding whether an authority spread ratio clears the competitiveness floor, gating whether a lever counts as genuinely contesting the decision.

nodes.name: variance_commit_threshold
nodes.summary: Resolves the variance-space commitment threshold from the configured value, implementing the 2026-03-18 fix that moved commitment out of precision space.

nodes.name: compute_action_object_alignment_bias
nodes.summary: Computes a per-candidate scoring bias from how well each candidate action aligns with the supplied action-object bias vector, weighted by a configurable strength.

nodes.name: field.py
nodes.summary: Implements the residue field phi(z_world): an RBF-based, non-erasable accumulation of the ethical cost of world-changes the agent caused, plus a parallel benefit terrain of positive attractors. Read by E3, the hippocampal module and others.
nodes.languageNotes: Radial-basis-function layer over a latent space, with an EWC anchor mechanism to protect accumulated residue against catastrophic forgetting.

nodes.name: RBFLayer
nodes.summary: Radial-basis-function layer storing residue centres with per-centre bandwidths and valences; supports adding single or clustered residues, local density computation and sensitization-gain updates.

nodes.name: ResidueField
nodes.summary: The residue field proper: evaluates harm residue, benefit terrain and safety over z_world, enforces the hypothesis-tag refusal so simulated content cannot accumulate residue, and provides EWC anchoring against forgetting.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: The single canonical configuration surface for every REE-v3 component -- latent stack, E1/E2/E3 predictors, event segmenter, hippocampal subsystem, residue, heartbeat and environment -- aggregated by the top-level REEConfig with size presets and derived-dimension factories.
nodes.languageNotes: A very large stack of frozen-style dataclasses; REEConfig.from_dims is the main factory and deliberately owns cross-component dimension consistency.

nodes.name: derive_stdlib_rng_seed
nodes.summary: Derives a distinct, reproducible per-consumer seed from a base seed and a stream id, so two stdlib-random consumers seeded from the same base never draw correlated sequences.

nodes.name: _register_observed_config
nodes.summary: Records each constructed config object into a module-level registry, giving experiment tooling a record of which configuration instances were actually observed at runtime.

nodes.name: LatentStackConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the latent stack, including the SD-005 split of z_gamma into self_dim (proprioceptive/interoceptive) and world_dim (exteroceptive) channels and the encoder/harm-bridge options over them.

nodes.name: E1Config
nodes.summary: Configuration for the E1 deep predictor, covering its context memory, training schedule and the many gated behavioural options it exposes to experiments.

nodes.name: E2Config
nodes.summary: Configuration for the E2 fast predictor, including the action_object_dim added for SD-004 action objects.

nodes.name: E3Config
nodes.summary: The largest component config: every knob of the E3 trajectory selector, including dynamic precision via prediction-error variance (ARC-016), commitment thresholds, residue weighting and candidate-generation options.

nodes.name: EventSegmenterScaleConfig
nodes.summary: Per-scale parameters for one timescale of the multi-scale event segmenter.

nodes.name: EventSegmenterConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the event segmenter that cuts experience into event boundaries, aggregating one or more scale configs.

nodes.name: InvalidationTriggerConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the triggers that invalidate a held goal or anchor when the world diverges from expectation.

nodes.name: AnchorSetConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the hippocampal anchor set: capacity, admission and eviction policy, and the payload fields carried per anchor.

nodes.name: StalenessAccumulatorConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the staleness accumulator that ages anchors and goals toward reconsideration.

nodes.name: GhostGoalBankConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the ghost goal bank that retains dropped goals for later persistence appraisal and possible revival.

nodes.name: PersistenceAppraisalComputeConfig
nodes.summary: Small config selecting how persistence appraisal is computed for banked ghost goals.

nodes.name: HippocampalConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the hippocampal module that navigates action-object space O (SD-004), covering replay, landscape reads of residue and benefit terrain, and anchor/ghost-goal integration.

nodes.name: ResidueConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the residue field: RBF bandwidths and capacity, accumulation gates, EWC anchoring, and the benefit-terrain switch (ARC-030, MECH-117).

nodes.name: HeartbeatConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the multi-rate clock and heartbeat cadence (SD-006) that paces the agent's subsystems.

nodes.name: EnvironmentConfig
nodes.summary: Minimal configuration describing the environment the agent is embedded in, such as observation and action dimensions.

nodes.name: REEConfig
nodes.summary: Top-level aggregate configuration composing every component config, with a __post_init__ consistency pass, feature-cluster enablers (sleep aggregation, goal stream) and the from_dims / large / xlarge factory presets.

nodes.name: salience_coordinator.py
nodes.summary: Implements the SD-032a salience-network coordinator that binds the cingulate subdivisions into a single network, emitting a soft operating-mode probability vector over external_task / internal_planning / internal_replay / offline_consolidation plus a mode-switch trigger. Also hosts the MECH-261 mode-conditioned per-target write-gate registry.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure-arithmetic, non-trainable PyTorch-adjacent module: no gradient flow, state is reset at episode boundaries, and the mode vector is produced by an explicit softmax over affinity logits rather than a learned head.

nodes.name: bound_affinity_input
nodes.summary: Bounds a single raw affinity-input signal to a configured cap using either the legacy box clamp or a smooth squash (cap * value / (sigma + |value|)). Kept at module level so contract tests and diagnostic drivers can exercise the operator without constructing a coordinator.

nodes.name: SalienceCoordinatorConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding every tunable of the salience coordinator: per-signal mode-affinity weights, salience weights, softmax temperature and stability-temperature options, enter/exit hysteresis thresholds, and affinity-input bounding parameters. Defaults are chosen to be backward-compatible with the pre-existing waking baseline.

nodes.name: SalienceCoordinator
nodes.summary: Stateful coordinator that accumulates named input signals from the cingulate subdivisions, computes a soft operating-mode vector each tick, applies hysteresis to the discrete mode, and fires a mode_switch_trigger when the salience aggregate crosses threshold. Exposes per-target write gates, diagnostics and reset for episode boundaries.

nodes.name: phase_manager.py
nodes.summary: Drives the SD-017 sleep cycle for the REE agent: tracks episodes and waking steps since the last cycle, decides when to enter sleep, and orchestrates the SWS/REM/writeback phase walk across the replay sampler, routing gate, Bayesian and self-model aggregators, and cross-module consolidator. Central coordination point for the entire sleep-aggregation cluster (Phases A-E).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses TYPE_CHECKING-only imports for all collaborators, so the module has zero runtime import coupling; collaborators are injected through the constructor and accessed defensively via getattr, keeping every sub-feature inert when its flag is off.

nodes.name: SleepPhase
nodes.summary: Enum defining the canonical sleep phase ordering: WAKING, SLEEP_ENTRY, SWS_ANALOG, PHASE_SWITCH, REM_ANALOG and WRITEBACK. Several members are reserved tokens populated by later cluster phases.

nodes.name: SleepCycleState
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding per-cycle bookkeeping: cycle index, current phase, episodes and waking steps since the last sleep, and the last emitted metrics dict. Reset at the start of every sleep cycle.

nodes.name: SleepLoopManager
nodes.summary: Deterministic K-episode driver for the SD-017 sleep cycle that also supports the within-life step-based and MEL-adaptive entry triggers. Runs the SWS and REM replay passes, routes draws through the routing gate into the Bayesian and self-model aggregators, performs precision recalibration, residue integration and cross-module consolidation, and emits a merged per-cycle metrics dict.
nodes.languageNotes: Marked welfare_relevant = True as a descriptive ethics-perimeter marker (SENT-0), not a runtime gate.

nodes.name: SleepLoopManager.__init__
nodes.summary: Validates and stores the large configuration surface for the sleep loop -- cadence, replay draws, aggregator wiring, REM precision recalibration, residue integration, MEL consumer and consolidation knobs -- and initialises the per-cycle state.

nodes.name: SleepLoopManager.notify_episode_end
nodes.summary: Increments the episode counter at the end of each waking episode and fires a sleep cycle when the configured cadence is reached, consulting the MEL consumer for adaptive entry permission.

nodes.name: SleepLoopManager.notify_waking_step
nodes.summary: Per-waking-step hook implementing the within-life sleep trigger: accumulates steps since last sleep, reads MEL need and entry-pressure crossings, records the trigger diagnostics, and runs a cycle when a threshold is crossed.

nodes.name: SleepLoopManager.reset
nodes.summary: Clears cycle state and history back to a fresh WAKING baseline and resets the MEL consumer, used between runs or seeds.

nodes.name: SleepLoopManager._run_cycle
nodes.summary: Executes one complete sleep cycle: checks the onset permit, walks SWS and REM phases drawing and routing replay samples into the Bayesian and self-model aggregators, invokes the agent's run_sleep_cycle, applies REM precision recalibration, residue integration and cross-module consolidation, then merges all sub-module metrics and appends the cycle to history.

nodes.name: SleepLoopManager._build_evidence_snapshot
nodes.summary: Assembles the per-cycle evidence snapshot by merging the scientist-agent buffer's evidence with the staleness accumulator's snapshot, used as the lookup source for aggregator updates.

nodes.name: SleepLoopManager._extract_region_key
nodes.summary: Defensively derives a hashable region key from a routed replay event, tolerating several payload shapes so replayed-region tracking never raises.

nodes.name: SleepLoopManager._lookup_evidence
nodes.summary: Looks up the evidence value for a routed event in the cycle's evidence snapshot, falling back through several key shapes and coercing the result to float.
